title: Finite-stalk evaluation and Frobenius return for a finite compactification
statement: For a finite compactification c=(j,p) of a morphism f₀ of finite-type k₀-schemes, with quasi-separated target, let F be an actual constructible common-stage Weil sheaf. Fix a closed target point y, a finite Weil presentation K of the specified R⁰p_*j!F, and a k₀-embedding of κ(y) into the fixed closure. Its scalar-extended degree-zero stalk admits a finite jointly injective family of linear evaluation maps into scalar-extended stalks of finite Weil presentations of F at closed x above y. Each evaluation has a positive return degree e, satisfies #κ(x)=#κ(y)^e, and intertwines F_y^e with the specified local operator F_x. The operators are the recorded finite-stage localClosedFrobeniusCohomology operators. This is a statement about vectors and operators, with no eigenvalue or weight hypotheses or conclusions.

proof.text: Choose an affine target neighbourhood V₀ of y. The framework/PBC open exchange identifies restriction of the specified higher image with the finite compactification over V₀, including its Weil structure. Put B=j_{V!}(F|_{X_V}). The weight-free stalk clause of [lem-zl-immersion-weil-local-behavior] identifies its stalk and local Frobenius at every source point with those of F, and gives zero stalks off the source. A point of X_{V₀} with residue field finite over k₀ is closed also in X₀, by [lem-kun-closed-point-field]. No complex embedding or weight hypothesis is introduced.

source.place: Paragraph (2), open-immersion stalk argument; applied using the weight-free immersion statement and the original arbitrary embedding

proof.text: The finite-image germ isomorphism identifies the target stalk with the finite geometric-stalk sum. The finite Weil-sections decomposition over κ(y) gives cycles of positive degree e=[κ(x):κ(y)]. Its return identity and the pullback/local-Frobenius comparison identify F_y^e on the component with the recorded F_x. A residue-field basis gives #κ(x)=#κ(y)^e. Remove the zero stalks off the source open, retaining joint injectivity. Choose finite Weil presentations together with the supplied output presentation and their comparison equations; scalar extension and normalized stage transport carry these evaluation maps and return identities to the operators in the statement. The empty fibre is the empty evaluation family on a zero vector space.

theorem sfFiniteCompactificationStalkReturn
[QuasiSeparated Y₀.hom] (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀) (c : Compactification f₀.left)
    [IsFinite c.g] (F : sfCommonStageWeilSheaf D l hl X₀ Ω)
    (y : {y : Y₀.left // y ∈ closedPoints Y₀.left})
    (L : Padic.FiniteCoefficientFields l Ω)
    (K : sfWeilComplex D l hl Y₀ (AlgebraicallyClosedCoefficients.Coefficient.{u} l Ω L))
    (hK : Nonempty ((zlWeilHigherShriek D l hl Ω f₀ c 0 F).obj ≅
      sfWeilStageObject D l hl Y₀ Ω L K))
    (ι : Y₀.left.residueField y.val →+* D.k)
    (hι : ι.comp (Y₀.hom.residueFieldAlgebraMap y.val) = algebraMap D.k₀ D.k) :
    Nonempty (SfFiniteCompactificationStalkReturn D l hl Ω f₀ F y L K ι hι)
